understand.concept: A set comprehension builds a set from an iterable with an expression and optional condition. It automatically removes duplicates. Use it when uniqueness is part of the desired result, not when order or duplicate counts matter.
understand.whyItMatters: Set Comprehensions and Practical Patterns is useful when a program needs to organize, inspect or transform related data reliably.
understand.analogy: A set is like a collection of unique membership cards: each item is present once, with no positional promise.
understand.analogyLimit: A set does not preserve a meaningful position for each member, and elements must be hashable.

explain.narrative:
## Set Comprehensions and Practical Patterns

A set comprehension builds a set from an iterable with an expression and optional condition. It automatically removes duplicates. Use it when uniqueness is part of the desired result, not when order or duplicate counts matter.

## Choosing an operation

Read the example code and check whether the operation mutates the object, returns a new value, or may raise an exception. Use membership tests and defaults where input may be missing.

## Practical reasoning

The five examples progress from basic use to a small real-world pattern. Compare each expected output with the code before changing it.
